quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: Computer hardware engineers research, design, develop or test computer or computer-related equipment, and may supervise its manufacturing and installation.

quick_facts.label: Other names for it
quick_facts.value: Job titles O*NET reports for this occupation (Computer Hardware Engineers) include Hardware Design Engineer, Hardware Engineer, Physical Design Engineer and Design Engineer.

quick_facts.label: Typical preparation
quick_facts.value: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.

sections.heading: What a hardware design engineer does
paragraphs: Computer hardware engineers research, design, develop or test computer or computer-related equipment, and may supervise its manufacturing and installation.

The tasks below are taken from the O*NET profile for Computer Hardware Engineers. O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Design and develop computer hardware and supporting peripherals, including central processing units.
Build, test and modify product prototypes using working or simulated models.
Write functional specifications that document the hardware development process.
Test and verify that hardware meets its specifications and requirements.

sections.heading: How people get into this job
paragraphs: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.
In India, the UGC specification of degrees lists B.Tech and B.E. as four-year bachelor's degrees entered after 10+2.
O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Common routes into this job on the Career Tree map: B.Tech in Electronics and Communication Engineering; B.Tech in Electrical Engineering; M.Tech in Electronics and Communication Engineering; Chip Design Engineer.
